title: Kubernetes Secret manifest served in a response
description: The body is a Kubernetes Secret object (kind: Secret with a data or stringData block). Secret values are base64-encoded rather than encrypted, so anything that serves this object publishes the credentials it holds to anyone who can request the path.
remediation: Remove the manifest from any served path, revoke the exposed credentials, and deliver secrets through the cluster API or an external secret store rather than through build output.
limitation: One response body. The check recognises the manifest shape; it does not decode or use the values.

observation.body:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db
 type: Opaque
data:
  password: cGxhY2Vob2xkZXItdmFsdWU=

kind: Secret
apiVersion: v1
stringData:
  token: placeholder-value
  user: app

apiVersion: v1
kind: Config
clusters:
  - name: prod
    cluster:
      server: https://k8s.example:6443

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api
spec:
  replicas: 2
